name: ATM expired-reward reserve-removal campaign
summary: Staking.burnExpiredReward was permissionless and converted any expired USDT-denominated reward into an ATM amount at the current pair reserves. It then called ATMToken.recycle, which transferred ATM directly from the ATM/USDT pair to Staking and synchronized the reduced ATM reserve. The attacker repeated this reserve removal to raise ATM's apparent price, then sold through 30 farmer contracts; ATMToken's sell branch amplified the cashout by auto-selling contract-held ATM with no minimum output.
notes: setATM changed Staking's ATM pointer in slot 2 to the implicated token. This made burnExpiredReward's permissionless reserve-removal path target the ATM/USDT pair; the pointer remained unchanged through the campaign.

ATMToken's constructor fixed STAKING to 0xa479bdcd0eed3a776a4fefe5e13899bab567f263 and created the ATM/USDT pair. No executable-code or later causal state change replaced recycle's authority or reserve-removal logic before exploitation.

Across the eight campaign setup and cashout transactions, ATM/USDT pair Transfer logs show 381,343.544327480794650401 USDT out and 200,018.979935764085407782 USDT of attacker-supplied inputs, leaving exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 181,324.564391716709242619 USDT. The pair balance from immediately before the first setup transaction through the final cashout changes by the same amount. The 130 intervening reserve-removal transactions move ATM rather than USDT. No recovery is netted.
Not the knot: one link of the conjunctive failure; the sibling with the latest age reset supplies the incident's single observation.
